item.title: Myanmar: Poverty deepens as families face multiple shocks with limited resources
item.description: Years of conflict, displacement, economic disruption and climate shocks in Myanmar have led to the “simultaneous collapse” of shelter, healthcare, schooling and livelihoods affecting millions of people, the UN Development Programme (UNDP) said in a report issued on Thursday.

item.title: ‘Overshoot is not a reason to surrender’: UN calls for accelerated climate action ahead of COP31 summit
item.description: As world leaders prepare for November’s major COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, record-breaking heat, devastating floods and an unprecedented El Niño climate pattern are making global climate action ever more urgent.

item.title: UN rights chief: Legacy of slavery and colonialism is still fuelling racism
item.description: The legacy of enslavement and colonialism continues to shape the lives of Africans and people of African descent, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday, calling for urgent action to deliver reparatory justice beyond financial compensation.

item.title: ‘Age must never diminish rights,’ UN independent expert warns
item.description: Older women around the world face violence, exploitation and neglect, yet remain largely invisible in the laws, policies, data and services designed to protect women overall, a UN independent human rights expert said on Thursday.

item.title: Afghanistan: Women face fresh dress code arrests amid record refugee returns
item.description: Afghan women and girls are being arrested, detained and threatened with arrest by Taliban authorities, the UN warned on Thursday as record numbers of returnees struggle to rebuild their lives back home.

item.title: World News in Brief: Russian attacks continue in Ukraine, Gazans shelter in flood-prone areas, keeping sight of eye health
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Thursday he was appalled by a wave of attacks that have killed civilians across Ukraine over the past four days.

item.title: Darfur: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
item.description: More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

item.title: Smartphone Ban Robs Afghan Female Journalists of a Vital Working Tool
item.description: The author is an Afghanistan-based female journalist, trained with Finnish support before the Taliban take-over. Her identity is withheld for security reasons
